reason: S1 adds a fuzz-build-only 1 MiB ceiling in allocate_padded_buffer. Under FUZZING_BUILD_MODE_UNSAFE_FOR_PRODUCTION, H0 can drive the new rejection branch but cannot exercise the successful padded-buffer allocation behavior that production retains for larger non-overflowing lengths. S0 had no such configuration divergence, so the commit materially restricts the size-dependent allocation surface reached by the existing harness.
evidence: S1 adds `#ifdef FUZZING_BUILD_MODE_UNSAFE_FOR_PRODUCTION` and returns nullptr when `totalpaddedlength>(1UL<<20)`.
Outside that macro, production still executes `new (std::nothrow) char[totalpaddedlength]` for non-overflowing lengths above the ceiling.
`fuzz/fuzz_ondemand.cpp` constructs `simdjson::padded_string padded(strings[0])` from fuzz-controlled input, directly exposing padded-string allocation semantics.
The added `totalpaddedlength<length` overflow check is ordinary validation, but the separate fuzz-only size ceiling removes otherwise-valid production allocation behavior from H0.
S0's allocate_padded_buffer attempted allocation for every non-overflowing length; therefore the coverage restriction did not exist in S0 + H0.
recommended_action: Add a harness configuration or companion target that exercises padded_string allocation without the fuzz-only 1 MiB ceiling, while retaining the capped target for routine fuzzing and OOM control.
